title: Escrowed activation with holdpoints and replayable rollback plan for Optimize suggestions
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Goal: Implement an escrowed activation flow that lets Optimize suggestions (batching/caching configs) be automatically proposed and partially enacted behind operator holdpoints. Each activation must include a replayable revert bundle so we can reliably roll back multi-part config changes across Dedicated and Private deployments. This ticket covers the orchestration layer, holdpoint API, approval signals, and the minimal safety checks required prior to progressive ramping.
background: Optimize currently generates recommendations for batching and KV caching profiles. Engineering has built pilot autoapply flows, but we need a robust production-safe activation orchestration that supports: operator escrow (human-in-the-loop approval with policy constraints), pre-commit validation (schema, compatibility, simulation), staged ramping (synthetic-traffic canaries and percentage-based traffic shifts), and a guaranteed rollback path that can be executed automatically or manually with forensic context.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Holdpoint API that registers an activation and pauses final commit until an approved signal or timeout. 2) Each activation produces an immutable revert bundle (git-like patch + metadata + telemetry snapshot). 3) Canary runner that can run synthetic traffic for any activation and report pass/fail metrics. 4) Rollback executor that applies revert bundle across same targets and verifies parity. 5) Operator UI hooks in Console for approve/reject/force-rollback with links to telemetry and PRs. 6) Automated tests and a dry-run mode that simulates the full flow in staging.
work_items: Define holdpoint API and protobufs for activation lifecycle
Extend Optimize recommender to emit activation manifest with revert bundle stub
Implement escrow store (encrypted, indexed) for pending activations
Build canary runner component for synthetic traffic and metric assertions
Integrate Console UI controls for holdpoint approvals and escalation notes
Create rollback executor service that replays revert bundles and validates outcomes
Add audit trail and tamper-evidence (signatures) for all activations
telemetry_requirements: Capture token-level latency, 95/99 latency percentiles, error rates, model fallback occurrences, batch size distribution, KV cache hit rates before/during/after activation. Snapshot pre-activation baseline and persist for 14 days. Canary runs must log per-request traces and pass/fail assertions.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag the holdpoint flow behind optimize.autoapply.escrow in staging. 2) Run internal service rollout for 2 internal teams with dry-run only for 1 week. 3) Enable synthetic canaries: 1% traffic synthetic for first 4 hours, then 10% for 24 hours, then progressive 25/50/100 with health checks at each stage. 4) For Dedicated customers, default to manual approval unless opted-in. 5) Gate production activation on green canary and operator approval or automated safety pass.
testing_strategy: Unit tests for API, property tests for revert bundle application, e2e in staging with mirrored traffic, chaos tests to simulate partial failure during commit and rollback, canary assertion suite including latency regression guardrails. Include a simulated operator script that approves, delays, and forces rollback to validate behavior.
rollback_playbook: 1) If a canary fails, auto-suspend further ramp and notify on-call with runbook link. 2) Run rollback executor with revert bundle ID; verify config diff is reverted. 3) Re-run the last-known-good canary to validate recovery. 4) Create incident with telemetry snapshot and link to revert bundle. 5) If rollback fails, escalate to runtime-team with a forced cold-restart and manual config replacement instructions.
security_considerations: Escrow store must encrypt activation manifests at rest and require KMS keys per-tenant for Private deployments. Approval endpoints require RBAC checks and audit-logged operator identities. Revert bundles must be signed and verified before application.
